# Data Preparation
Here the data is loaded from the saved TCGA-BRCA data. We identified the primary tumor and normal samples. Following this, the protein-coding genes were selected.

```{r tcga_data_acquisition, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#################################################################################
#### Cancer data set ############################################################
#################################################################################

#######################
#### Load packages ####
#######################
# BiocManager::install("TCGAbiolinks")
# BiocManager::install("EDASeq") # required for sample normalization
library(TCGAbiolinks); library(EDASeq)


##########################################
#### Load saved TCGA-BRCA data ####
##########################################
data <- readRDS("TCGA_BRCA_SummarizedExperiment.rds")
dataPrimary_Target <- colnames(data)[data$shortLetterCode == "TP"]
dataNormal_Target  <- colnames(data)[data$shortLetterCode == "NT"]

dim(data)
length(dataPrimary_Target)
length(dataNormal_Target)
 

############################################
#### Subset summarizedExperiment object ####
############################################
SECoding <- data[rowData(data)$gene_type == "protein_coding", ]

#############################################################################################################
#### The following function will return the data from specified slots in the summarizedExperiment object ####
#############################################################################################################
dataPrep_Coding <- TCGAanalyze_Preprocessing(object = SECoding, cor.cut = 0.6,  datatype = "unstranded")                      

########################################
#### quantile normalize the samples ####
########################################
dataNorm_Coding <- TCGAanalyze_Normalization(
  tabDF = dataPrep_Coding,
  geneInfo = geneInfoHT,
  method = "geneLength"
)


########################
#### Filter samples ####
########################
dataFilt_Coding <- TCGAanalyze_Filtering(tabDF = dataNorm_Coding, method = "quantile", qnt.cut =  0.25)   

 
```
## Normalization Comparison
Expression distributions were compared before and after normalization to assess whether preprocessing reduced sample-level technical variability.


```{r q1_normalization_comparison, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}

old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2),
  mar = c(4, 4, 4, 2)
)


boxplot(
  log2(dataPrep_Coding + 1),
  outline = FALSE,
 col = "lightskyblue",
border = "grey65",
medcol = "navy",
  names = FALSE,
  main = "Expression Before Normalization",
  xlab = "TCGA-BRCA Samples",
  ylab = "log2(expression + 1)",
  ylim = c(0, 24),
)

boxplot(
  log2(dataNorm_Coding + 1),
  outline = FALSE,
  col = "lightskyblue",
border = "grey65",
medcol = "navy",
  names = FALSE,
  main = "Expression After Normalization",
  xlab = "TCGA-BRCA Samples",
  ylab = "log2(expression + 1)",
  ylim = c(0, 24),
)
par(old_par)


```
The overall distributions appear similar before and after normalization with no large visual shift. We cannot claim that technical effects were removed based solely on this.



## Initial Data Inspection

Firstly, we checked the dataset dimensions, Tumor and Normal counts along with gene annotations and missing values. These checks help identify potential errors in the downstream analysis. Also we want to make sure we have an idea of what we have in counts to assess group balance and available statistical power. We want to make sure in the annotations that we match gene IDs to gene symbols consistently.
```{r week1_data_inspection}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(matrixStats)

# Inspect available expression assays
assayNames(data)

# Extract raw, unstranded STAR counts for protein-coding genes
coding_counts <- assay(
  SECoding,
  "unstranded"
)

# Extract matching sample and gene information
sample_info <- as.data.frame(
  colData(SECoding)
)

gene_info <- as.data.frame(
  rowData(SECoding)
)

# Verify alignment
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(coding_counts),
    rownames(sample_info)
  ),
  identical(
    rownames(coding_counts),
    rownames(gene_info)
  )
)

# Create the analysis-group variable
sample_info$Group <- factor(
  sample_info$sample_type,
  levels = c(
    "Solid Tissue Normal",
    "Primary Tumor"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "Normal",
    "Tumor"
  )
)
# Log2-transform raw counts for visualization (+1 avoids log2(0))
log_counts <- log2(coding_counts + 1)

# Inspect the data dimensions and sample balance
dim(coding_counts)
table(sample_info$Group)

head(
  sample_info[
    ,
    c(
      "barcode",
      "sample_type",
      "preservation_method",
      "Group"
    )
  ]
)

head(
  gene_info[
    ,
    c(
      "gene_name",
      "gene_type"
    )
  ]
)

# Build the tables
column_stats <- data.frame(
  Library_Size = colSums(coding_counts)
)

row_stats <- data.frame(
  Mean = rowMeans(log_counts),
  SD   = rowSds(log_counts)
)

# Check for missing expression measurements
sum(is.na(coding_counts))
```

```{r week1_expression_distributions, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
group_colors <- ifelse(
  sample_info$Group == "Tumor",
  "tomato",
  "steelblue"
)

boxplot(

  outline = FALSE,
  names = FALSE,
  col = group_colors,
  main = "Raw Log2 Expression Distributions",
  xlab = "TCGA-BRCA Samples",

)

legend(

```
Most samples have broad but similar expression distributions while a few appear shifted. The groups are not clearly separated and the Normal and Tumor distributions overlap substantially.
```{r week1_library_sizes, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
barplot(
  column_stats$Library_Size / 1e6,
  names.arg = FALSE,
  col = group_colors,
  border = NA,
  main = "Protein-Coding Library Sizes by Sample",
  xlab = "TCGA-BRCA Samples",
  ylab = "Protein-coding reads (millions)"
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("Normal", "Tumor"),
  fill = c("steelblue", "tomato"),
  bty = "n"
)
```
We have in our visualization the comparison of library sizes. The library sizes across tumor and normal samples are mostly consistent with each other while there are a few that have noticeably more reads. Differences in read depth can affect raw expression counts. 
```{r week1_mean_sd, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
plot(
  row_stats$Mean,
  row_stats$SD,
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.35,
  col = rgb(
    0.15,
    0.35,
    0.65,
```

In the Variability vs Gene-Level Mean we see that variability rises from low expression and spreads widely at intermediate expression, generally decreasing at higher expression. We also can see that a dense group of highly expressed genes has relatively low variability. 

## Gene Selection for PCA
Here we log2-transform the filtered, normalized expression data and then calculate each gene’s variance across samples. Then it selects the 100 and 1,000 most variable genes for PCA. We confirm the resulting matrix sizes with dimension checks. Variable genes help reveal the differences among samples even though high variance alone doesn't establish biological importance or predictive value.
```{r q1, fig.width=14, fig.height=7}
################################################################################
################################################################################
#### Part 1 PCA ################################################################
################################################################################
################################################################################

#### Select probes by variance ####
ge = log2(dataFilt_Coding + 1)
gene_variance <- apply(
  ge,
  1,
  var
)

variance_order <- order(
  gene_variance,
  decreasing = TRUE
)

 top100 <- ge[
  variance_order[1:100],
]

  top1000 <- ge[
  variance_order[1:1000],
]

 
dim(top100)
dim(top1000)
```

```{r gene_age_correlations}
# One tumor sample per patient, with age available
keep_age <- sample_info$Group == "Tumor" &
  !is.na(sample_info$age_at_diagnosis)

age_info <- sample_info[keep_age, , drop = FALSE]
age_info <- age_info[!duplicated(age_info$patient), , drop = FALSE]

age_years <- age_info$age_at_diagnosis / 365.25
age_ge <- ge[, rownames(age_info), drop = FALSE]

# Spearman correlations for each gene
age_results <- t(apply(age_ge, 1, function(values) {
  if (sd(values) == 0) {
    return(c(rho = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_))
  }

  result <- cor.test(
    values, age_years,
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )

  c(rho = unname(result$estimate), p_value = result$p.value)
}))

age_results <- data.frame(
  ID = rownames(age_results),
  age_results,
  row.names = NULL
)

age_results$padj <- p.adjust(age_results$p_value, method = "BH")

gene_match <- match(
  sub("\\..*$", "", age_results$ID),
  sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
)
age_results$Gene <- gene_info$gene_name[gene_match]

nrow(age_info)

age_results |>
  dplyr::select(ID, Gene, rho, p_value, padj) |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj, p_value) |>
  head(10)

sum(age_results$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```
The Spearman correlations were calculated between each gene's expression and age in years. Benjamini–Hochberg correction was applied to account for testing many genes, and gene symbols were added for readability.  There were 104 patients with no significant genes after correction in the Age analysis. CDO1 had the strongest listed association but did not remain significant. There is one tumor sample per patient with age available.

```{r gene_time_correlations}
# One tumor sample per patient
tumor_info <- sample_info[
  sample_info$Group == "Tumor", , drop = FALSE
]
tumor_info <- tumor_info[
  !duplicated(tumor_info$patient), , drop = FALSE
]

time_variables <- c(
  "days_to_death",
  "days_to_last_follow_up"
)

time_results <- list()

for (variable in time_variables) {
  info <- tumor_info[
    !is.na(tumor_info[[variable]]), , drop = FALSE
  ]

  values <- info[[variable]]
  expression <- ge[, rownames(info), drop = FALSE]

  results <- t(apply(expression, 1, function(gene) {
    if (length(values) < 3 ||
        sd(values) == 0 ||
        sd(gene) == 0) {
      return(c(rho = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_))
    }

    test <- cor.test(
      gene, values,
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )

    c(rho = unname(test$estimate), p_value = test$p.value)
  }))

  results <- data.frame(
    ID = rownames(results),
    results,
    row.names = NULL
  )

  results$padj <- p.adjust(results$p_value, method = "BH")

  gene_match <- match(
    sub("\\..*$", "", results$ID),
    sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
  )
  results$Gene <- gene_info$gene_name[gene_match]

  time_results[[variable]] <- results

  cat("\nVariable:", variable,
      "\nPatients:", nrow(info), "\n")

  print(
    results |>
      dplyr::select(ID, Gene, rho, p_value, padj) |>
      dplyr::arrange(padj, p_value) |>
      head(10)
  )

  cat("BH-significant genes:",
      sum(results$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
}
```

The days-to-death analysis included only 11 patients and identified 134 BH-significant genes; this finding requires caution because of the small sample. The Last follow-up group has 111 patients with no BH-significant genes. In our time analysis, these correlations do not account for censoring and therefore aren't survival analyses.

## Most and Least Variable Genes


```{r gene_variance}
library(dplyr)

sample_cols <- colnames(ge)

expression_df <- as.data.frame(ge) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("ID")

row_stats <- expression_df |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    row_mean = mean(c_across(all_of(sample_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    row_sd = sd(c_across(all_of(sample_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    row_variance = var(c_across(all_of(sample_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
# Match gene IDs, removing any version suffix
gene_match <- match(
  sub("\\..*$", "", row_stats$ID),
  sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
)

row_stats$Gene <- gene_info$gene_name[gene_match]
# Ten genes with the highest variance
row_stats |>
  select(ID, Gene, row_mean, row_sd, row_variance) |>
  arrange(desc(row_variance)) |>
  head(10)

# Ten genes with the lowest variance
row_stats |>
  select(ID, Gene, row_mean, row_sd, row_variance) |>
  arrange(row_variance) |>
  head(10)
```


This block calculates each gene's mean, standard deviation and variance. GSTM1 had the highest variance(~25.7), while DCTN2 had the lowest(~0.189). The variable genes can help reveal sample differences, but variance alone doesn't show whether a gene distinguishes Tumor from Normal.


```{r gene_gene_correlations}
gene_cor <- cor(t(top100), method = "spearman")

# Display a small corner of the matrix
round(gene_cor[1:5, 1:5], 3)

# One sample per patient for significance tests
unique_samples <- rownames(sample_info)[
  !duplicated(sample_info$patient)
]

pair_expression <- top100[, unique_samples, drop = FALSE]
gene_pairs <- combn(rownames(pair_expression), 2)

pair_results <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(gene_pairs)), function(i) {
  id1 <- gene_pairs[1, i]
  id2 <- gene_pairs[2, i]

  test <- cor.test(
    pair_expression[id1, ],
    pair_expression[id2, ],
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )

  data.frame(
    ID1 = id1,
    ID2 = id2,
    rho = unname(test$estimate),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
})

pair_results <- do.call(rbind, pair_results)
pair_results$padj <- p.adjust(pair_results$p_value, method = "BH")

annotation_ids <- sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)

pair_results$Gene1 <- gene_info$gene_name[
  match(sub("\\..*$", "", pair_results$ID1), annotation_ids)
]
pair_results$Gene2 <- gene_info$gene_name[
  match(sub("\\..*$", "", pair_results$ID2), annotation_ids)
]

pair_results |>
  dplyr::select(Gene1, Gene2, rho, p_value, padj) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(rho))) |>
  head(10)

sum(pair_results$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

The Spearman correlations measure how gene expression patterns vary together. The BH correction accounts for testing many gene pairs. The strongest listed correlation was between TRARG1 and CIDEC with ρ ≈ 0.986. The adjusted significance threshold was met by 4,068 pairs. We have to remember that strong correlation does not establish causation or direct regulation.

```{r metadata_correlations}
metadata <- data.frame(
  age_years = tumor_info$age_at_diagnosis / 365.25,
  days_to_death = tumor_info$days_to_death,
  follow_up_days = tumor_info$days_to_last_follow_up
)

metadata_pairs <- combn(names(metadata), 2)

metadata_results <- lapply(
  seq_len(ncol(metadata_pairs)),
  function(i) {
    variable1 <- metadata_pairs[1, i]
    variable2 <- metadata_pairs[2, i]

    complete <- complete.cases(
      metadata[, c(variable1, variable2)]
    )

    test <- cor.test(
      metadata[[variable1]][complete],
      metadata[[variable2]][complete],
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )

    data.frame(
      Variable1 = variable1,
      Variable2 = variable2,
      Patients = sum(complete),
      rho = unname(test$estimate),
      p_value = test$p.value
    )
  }
)

metadata_results <- do.call(rbind, metadata_results)
metadata_results$padj <- p.adjust(
  metadata_results$p_value,
  method = "BH"
)

metadata_results
```

This compares age, days to death and days to last follow-up using Spearman correlations and BH corrections. Age had no significant association with either time variable after correction. Days to death and last follow-up were perfectly correlated among 11 patients. This does not establish an independent biological relationship.

```{r pca_analysis}
#### PCA using top expression values ####

pca_top100 <- prcomp(
  t(top100),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)

pca_top1000 <- prcomp(
  t(top1000),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = TRUE
)


#### Calculate variance explained by PCA ####

summarize_pca_variance <- function(pca_object) {
  
  variance <- pca_object$sdev^2
  
  proportion <- variance / sum(variance)
  
  cumulative <- cumsum(proportion)
  
  data.frame(
    PC = seq_along(proportion),
    Proportion = proportion,
    Cumulative = cumulative
  )
}

variance_top100 <- summarize_pca_variance(
  pca_top100
)

variance_top1000 <- summarize_pca_variance(
  pca_top1000
)

#### Number of PCs required for 50% and 75% ####

pc_thresholds <- data.frame(
  Gene_Set = c("Top 100", "Top 1000"),
  
  PCs_for_50_percent = c(
    which(variance_top100$Cumulative >= 0.50)[1],
    which(variance_top1000$Cumulative >= 0.50)[1]
  ),
  
  PCs_for_75_percent = c(
    which(variance_top100$Cumulative >= 0.75)[1],
    which(variance_top1000$Cumulative >= 0.75)[1]
  )
)

pc_thresholds

head(variance_top100, 10)
head(variance_top1000, 10)
 

#### Plot PCA results ####
library(scatterplot3d)

# Arrange metadata in the same order as the PCA samples
pca_sample_info <- sample_info[
  rownames(pca_top100$x),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(pca_top100$x),
    rownames(pca_sample_info)
  )
)

# Colors identify phenotype
phenotype_colors <- c(
  Tumor = "#D55E00",
  Normal = "#0072B2"
)

point_colors <- phenotype_colors[
  as.character(pca_sample_info$Group)
]

# Shapes identify tissue preservation method
preservation_shapes <- c(
  FFPE    = 17,   # filled triangle, so the single FFPE sample stands out
  OCT     = 16,   # filled circle
  Unknown = 1     # open circle
)

point_shapes <- preservation_shapes[
  as.character(pca_sample_info$preservation_method)
]

# Function for calculating the percentage explained by each PC
pc_percent <- function(pca_object) {
  100 * pca_object$sdev^2 /
    sum(pca_object$sdev^2)
}

percent_top100 <- pc_percent(pca_top100)
percent_top1000 <- pc_percent(pca_top1000)



scatterplot3d(
  pca_top100$x[, 1],
  pca_top100$x[, 2],
  pca_top100$x[, 3],
  color = point_colors,
  pch = point_shapes,
  cex.symbols = 1.3,
  angle = 55,
  main = "PCA: Top 100 Variable Genes",
  xlab = paste0("PC1 (", round(percent_top100[1], 1), "%)"),
  ylab = paste0("PC2 (", round(percent_top100[2], 1), "%)"),
  zlab = paste0("PC3 (", round(percent_top100[3], 1), "%)")
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = names(phenotype_colors),
  col = phenotype_colors,
  pch = 16,
  title = "Phenotype",
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.8
)

scatterplot3d(
  pca_top1000$x[, 1],
  pca_top1000$x[, 2],
  pca_top1000$x[, 3],
  color = point_colors,
  pch = point_shapes,
  cex.symbols = 1.3,
  angle = 55,
  main = "PCA: Top 1000 Variable Genes",
  xlab = paste0("PC1 (", round(percent_top1000[1], 1), "%)"),
  ylab = paste0("PC2 (", round(percent_top1000[2], 1), "%)"),
  zlab = paste0("PC3 (", round(percent_top1000[3], 1), "%)")
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = names(phenotype_colors),
  col = phenotype_colors,
  pch = 16,
  title = "Phenotype",
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.8
)

legend(
  "topleft",
  legend =  
    names(preservation_shapes),
  
  pch = preservation_shapes,
  col = "black",
  title = "Preservation",
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.8
)


old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2),
  las = 2,
  cex.axis = 0.8
)

plot(
  pca_top100,
  type = "barplot",
  main = "Scree Plot: Top 100 Genes"
)

plot(
  pca_top1000,
  type = "barplot",
  main = "Scree Plot: Top 1,000 Genes"
)

par(old_par)
 

```

Here PCA summarizes expression patterns using the top 100 and 1,000 variable genes. The first two PCs explain 57.8% and 48.4% of the variance, respectively. These plots explore sample structure but do not establish predictive performance.
```{r q1_feature_selection}
################################################################################
################################################################################
#### Part 2 Logistic Regression ################################################
################################################################################
################################################################################


e.m = as.numeric(sample_info$Group == "Tumor")
sample.sel = rownames(sample_info) %in% colnames(ge)
sum(sample.sel) 
ge = ge[, rownames(sample_info)[sample.sel]]
e.m = e.m[sample.sel]
sum(e.m) 
stopifnot(identical(colnames(ge), rownames(sample_info)[sample.sel]))

e.m=factor(e.m,levels=c(0,1))
tt.pvals=apply(ge,1,function(x) t.test( x ~ e.m )$p.value )
hist(tt.pvals,col="lightgreen",breaks=50)
sort(tt.pvals)[1:5]


```
Feature selection uses two-sample t-tests to rank genes by differences between Tumor and Normal expression. Small p-values indicate evidence of a group difference, but they do not establish predictive performance by themselves.
```{r exploratory_heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Select the 20 genes with the smallest exploratory t-test p-values
heat_genes <- names(sort(tt.pvals))[1:20]
heat_data <- as.matrix(ge[heat_genes, , drop = FALSE])

# Match gene symbols
gene_labels <- gene_info$gene_name[
  match(
    sub("\\..*$", "", heat_genes),
    sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
  )
]
missing_labels <- is.na(gene_labels) | gene_labels == ""
gene_labels[missing_labels] <- heat_genes[missing_labels]

# Standardize each gene across samples
heat_z <- t(scale(t(heat_data)))

sample_colors <- ifelse(e.m == "1", "tomato", "steelblue")

heatmap(
  heat_z,
  scale = "none",
  col = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "tomato"))(101),
  ColSideColors = sample_colors,
  labRow = make.unique(gene_labels),
  labCol = NA,
  margins = c(5, 10),
  cexRow = 0.8,
  main = "Top 20 Genes: Exploratory Expression Heatmap"
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("Normal", "Tumor"),
  fill = c("steelblue", "tomato"),
  bty = "n",
  cex = 0.7
)
```
Here the exploratory heatmap displays the top 20 genes ranked by t-test p-value with expression standardized within each gene. Clustering shows mostly Tumor/Normal grouping with some mixing. This is an exploratory figure. It is not independent validation.

```{r q1_train_test_split}
set.seed(123)

# Align metadata with expression columns
model_info <- sample_info[colnames(ge), , drop = FALSE]

# Assign 80% of patients to training
patients <- unique(model_info$patient)
training_patients <- sample(
  patients,
  size = round(0.8 * length(patients))
)

train_idx <- which(model_info$patient %in% training_patients)
test_idx <- which(!model_info$patient %in% training_patients)

outcome <- factor(
  as.numeric(model_info$Group == "Tumor"),
  levels = c(0, 1)
)

# Rank genes using training samples only
training_pvals <- apply(ge[, train_idx, drop = FALSE], 1,
  function(values) {
    t.test(values ~ outcome[train_idx])$p.value
  }
)

top_genes <- names(sort(training_pvals))[1:2]

reg_df <- data.frame(
  e.m = outcome,
  gene1 = ge[top_genes[1], ],
  gene2 = ge[top_genes[2], ],
  row.names = colnames(ge)
)

train <- reg_df[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
test <- reg_df[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

gene_key <- data.frame(
  Model_Variable = c("gene1", "gene2"),
  Gene_ID = top_genes
)

gene_key$Symbol <- gene_info$gene_name[
  match(
    sub("\\..*$", "", top_genes),
    sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
  )
]

gene_key
table(train$e.m)
table(test$e.m)

# Verify no patient appears in both sets
stopifnot(
  length(intersect(
    model_info$patient[train_idx],
    model_info$patient[test_idx]
  )) == 0
)
assess.prediction=function(truth,predicted) {
# check for missing values (we are going to compute metrics
# on non-missing values of course)
predicted = predicted[ ! is.na(truth) ]
truth = truth[ ! is.na(truth) ]
truth = truth[ ! is.na(predicted) ]
predicted = predicted[ ! is.na(predicted) ]
cat("Total cases that are not NA: ",length(truth),"\n",sep="")
# overall accuracy of the test: how many cases (both positive and
# negative) we got right:
cat("Correct predictions (accuracy): ",sum(truth==predicted), "(",signif(sum(truth==predicted)*100/length(truth),3),"%)\n",sep="")
# how predictions align against known training/testing outcomes:
# TP/FP= true/false positives, TN/FN=true/false negatives:
TP = sum(truth==1 & predicted==1)
TN = sum(truth==0 & predicted==0)
FP = sum(truth==0 & predicted==1)
FN = sum(truth==1 & predicted==0)
P = TP+FN # total number of positives in the truth data
N = FP+TN # total number of negatives
cat("TPR (sensitivity)=TP/P: ", signif(100*TP/P,3),"%\n",sep="")
cat("TNR (specificity)=TN/N: ", signif(100*TN/N,3),"%\n",sep="")
cat("PPV (precision)=TP/(TP+FP): ", signif(100*TP/(TP+FP),3),"%\n",sep="")
cat("FDR (false discovery)=1-PPV: ", signif(100*FP/(TP+FP),3),"%\n",sep="")
cat("FPR =FP/N=1-TNR: ", signif(100*FP/N,3),"%\n",sep="")
}
 
# Model 1: top gene only
M1 <- glm(e.m ~ gene1, data = train, family = "binomial")

# Model 2: top two genes
M2 <- glm(
  e.m ~ gene1 + gene2,
  data = train,
  family = "binomial",
  control = glm.control(maxit = 100)
)
pred1 <- predict(M1, newdata = test, type = "response")
class1 <- as.numeric(pred1 > 0.5)

pred2 <- predict(M2, newdata = test, type = "response" )
class2 <- as.numeric(pred2 > 0.5)

summary(M1)
summary(M2)

assess.prediction(test$e.m, class1)
assess.prediction(test$e.m, class2)

anova(M1, M2, test = "Chisq")

rownames(test)[class1 != test$e.m]
cor.test(reg_df$gene1, reg_df$gene2)

"TCGA-A7-A0DC-01B-04R-A22O-07" %in% rownames(train)

cor(reg_df$gene1[reg_df$e.m == "1"], reg_df$gene2[reg_df$e.m == "1"])
cor(reg_df$gene1[reg_df$e.m == "0"], reg_df$gene2[reg_df$e.m == "0"])

knitr::kable(
  gene_key,
  caption = "Genes Selected for Logistic Regression"
)
```

The patients were divided approximately 80:20 between training and testing, keeping each patient's samples together to prevent leakage. The models learn from the training data and the held-out test data is used to assess their performance on unseen samples. This chunk also fits and compares one-gene and two-gene logistic regression models.

Our test model comparison compares the models’ performance on the same held-out test samples. Scores that are higher indicate that performance is better on this test set. However, small differences do not establish a clear winner. One-gene logistic regression had the highest test accuracy, 95.5% (42/44), while several other models performed better in cross-validation.


In patient-grouped cross validation we use five folds which keeps each patient's samples together and repeats feature selection within each training fold. This approach reduces leakage and assesses performance across multiple training/validation partitions.

```{r q2_grouped_cv, message=FALSE}
library(e1071)

set.seed(123)

# Use only the training patients
cv_info <- model_info[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
cv_expression <- ge[, train_idx, drop = FALSE]
cv_outcome <- outcome[train_idx]

# Keep all samples from a patient in the same fold
cv_patients <- unique(cv_info$patient)
patient_folds <- sample(
  rep(1:5, length.out = length(cv_patients))
)

sample_folds <- patient_folds[
  match(cv_info$patient, cv_patients)
]

cv_predictions <- data.frame(
  Truth = cv_outcome,
  Logistic_One_Probability = NA_real_,
  Logistic_Two_Probability = NA_real_,
  NB_One_Probability = NA_real_,
  NB_Two_Probability = NA_real_,
  row.names = colnames(cv_expression)
)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  fit_rows <- which(sample_folds != fold)
  validation_rows <- which(sample_folds == fold)

  # Select genes using this fold's training samples only
  fold_pvals <- apply(
    cv_expression[, fit_rows, drop = FALSE],
    1,
    function(values) {
      t.test(values ~ cv_outcome[fit_rows])$p.value
    }
  )

  fold_genes <- names(sort(fold_pvals))[1:2]

  fold_data <- data.frame(
    e.m = cv_outcome,
    gene1 = cv_expression[fold_genes[1], ],
    gene2 = cv_expression[fold_genes[2], ]
  )

  cv_train <- fold_data[fit_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  cv_test <- fold_data[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE]

  logistic_one <- glm(
    e.m ~ gene1,
    data = cv_train,
    family = binomial
  )

  logistic_two <- glm(
    e.m ~ gene1 + gene2,
    data = cv_train,
    family = binomial,
    control = glm.control(maxit = 100)
  )

  cv_predictions$Logistic_One_Probability[validation_rows] <-
    stats::predict(logistic_one, cv_test, type = "response")

  cv_predictions$Logistic_Two_Probability[validation_rows] <-
    stats::predict(logistic_two, cv_test, type = "response")

  nb_one <- naiveBayes(e.m ~ gene1, data = cv_train)
  nb_two <- naiveBayes(e.m ~ gene1 + gene2, data = cv_train)

  cv_predictions$NB_One_Probability[validation_rows] <-
    stats::predict(nb_one, cv_test, type = "raw")[, "1"]

  cv_predictions$NB_Two_Probability[validation_rows] <-
    stats::predict(nb_two, cv_test, type = "raw")[, "1"]
}

head(cv_predictions)

probability_cols <- names(cv_predictions)[-1]

for (model_name in probability_cols) {
  cat("\n", model_name, "\n")

  assess.prediction(
    cv_predictions$Truth,
    as.numeric(cv_predictions[[model_name]] > 0.5)
  )
}



```
## Random Forest Comparison

Random Forest compares mtry = 1 and mtry = 2. These control the number of genes that are considered at each tree split using patient-grouped cross-validation.
```{r random_forest_comparison, message=FALSE}
library(randomForest)

set.seed(123)

rf_cv_predictions <- matrix(
  NA_integer_,
  nrow = length(cv_outcome),
  ncol = 2,
  dimnames = list(
    names(cv_outcome),
    c("mtry_1", "mtry_2")
  )
)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  fit_rows <- which(sample_folds != fold)
  validation_rows <- which(sample_folds == fold)

  # Select genes within this fold's training data
  fold_pvals <- apply(
    cv_expression[, fit_rows, drop = FALSE],
    1,
    function(values) {
      t.test(values ~ cv_outcome[fit_rows])$p.value
    }
  )

  fold_genes <- names(sort(fold_pvals))[1:2]

  fold_data <- data.frame(
    e.m = cv_outcome,
    gene1 = cv_expression[fold_genes[1], ],
    gene2 = cv_expression[fold_genes[2], ]
  )

  cv_train <- fold_data[fit_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  cv_test <- fold_data[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE]

  for (m in 1:2) {

    forest <- randomForest(
      e.m ~ gene1 + gene2,
      data = cv_train,
      mtry = m,
      ntree = 500
    )

    predicted <- stats::predict(
      forest,
      newdata = cv_test,
      type = "class"
    )

    rf_cv_predictions[validation_rows, m] <-
      as.numeric(as.character(predicted))
  }
}

for (m in 1:2) {
  cat("\nRandom forest: mtry =", m, "\n")

  assess.prediction(
    cv_outcome,
    rf_cv_predictions[, m]
  )
}
```

## SVM Comparison

SVM compares a linear kernel with radial kernels by using different gamma settings to assess how these choices affect cross-validation performance.
```{r svm_comparison, message=FALSE}
library(e1071)

svm_settings <- data.frame(
  kernel = c("linear", "radial", "radial"),
  cost = c(1, 1, 1),
  gamma = c(0.5, 0.1, 1)
)

svm_cv_predictions <- matrix(
  NA_integer_,
  nrow = length(cv_outcome),
  ncol = nrow(svm_settings)
)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  fit_rows <- which(sample_folds != fold)
  validation_rows <- which(sample_folds == fold)

  # Select genes using this fold's training samples
  fold_pvals <- apply(
    cv_expression[, fit_rows, drop = FALSE],
    1,
    function(values) {
      t.test(values ~ cv_outcome[fit_rows])$p.value
    }
  )

  fold_genes <- names(sort(fold_pvals))[1:2]

  fold_data <- data.frame(
    e.m = cv_outcome,
    gene1 = cv_expression[fold_genes[1], ],
    gene2 = cv_expression[fold_genes[2], ]
  )

  cv_train <- fold_data[fit_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  cv_test <- fold_data[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE]

  for (j in seq_len(nrow(svm_settings))) {

    model <- svm(
      e.m ~ gene1 + gene2,
      data = cv_train,
      kernel = svm_settings$kernel[j],
      cost = svm_settings$cost[j],
      gamma = svm_settings$gamma[j],
      scale = TRUE
    )

    predicted <- stats::predict(model, newdata = cv_test)

    svm_cv_predictions[validation_rows, j] <-
      as.numeric(as.character(predicted))
  }
}

for (j in seq_len(nrow(svm_settings))) {
  cat(
    "\nSVM:", svm_settings$kernel[j],
    "| cost =", svm_settings$cost[j],
    "| gamma =", svm_settings$gamma[j], "\n"
  )

  assess.prediction(
    cv_outcome,
    svm_cv_predictions[, j]
  )
}
```

## Neural Network Comparison

This compares networks with zero vs five hidden units using patient grouped cross-validation.

```{r neural_network_comparison, message=FALSE}
library(neuralnet)

set.seed(123)

hidden_settings <- c(0, 5)

nn_cv_predictions <- matrix(
  NA_integer_,
  nrow = length(cv_outcome),
  ncol = length(hidden_settings)
)

for (fold in 1:5) {

  fit_rows <- which(sample_folds != fold)
  validation_rows <- which(sample_folds == fold)

  # Select genes using this fold's training samples
  fold_pvals <- apply(
    cv_expression[, fit_rows, drop = FALSE],
    1,
    function(values) {
      t.test(values ~ cv_outcome[fit_rows])$p.value
    }
  )

  fold_genes <- names(sort(fold_pvals))[1:2]

  predictors <- data.frame(
    gene1 = cv_expression[fold_genes[1], ],
    gene2 = cv_expression[fold_genes[2], ]
  )

  # Learn scaling within this fold
  scaled_fit <- scale(predictors[fit_rows, , drop = FALSE])

  scaled_validation <- scale(
    predictors[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE],
    center = attr(scaled_fit, "scaled:center"),
    scale = attr(scaled_fit, "scaled:scale")
  )

  fold_train <- as.data.frame(scaled_fit)
  fold_train$e.m <- as.numeric(
    as.character(cv_outcome[fit_rows])
  )

  for (j in seq_along(hidden_settings)) {

    network <- neuralnet(
      e.m ~ gene1 + gene2,
      data = fold_train,
      hidden = hidden_settings[j],
      linear.output = FALSE,
      stepmax = 1e6
    )

    if (is.null(network$result.matrix)) {
      stop(
        "Network did not converge: fold ", fold,
        ", hidden = ", hidden_settings[j]
      )
    }

    probability <- neuralnet::compute(
      network,
      as.data.frame(scaled_validation)
    )$net.result[, 1]

    nn_cv_predictions[validation_rows, j] <-
      as.numeric(probability > 0.5)
  }
}

for (j in seq_along(hidden_settings)) {
  cat(
    "\nNeural network: hidden =",
    hidden_settings[j], "\n"
  )

  assess.prediction(
    cv_outcome,
    nn_cv_predictions[, j]
  )
}
```


## Cross-validated performance

This summarizes cross-validation metrics for the logistic regression and Bayes models using predictions from held-out folds.

```{r q2_cross_validated_performance}
# Convert probabilities to predicted classes using 0.50 as the threshold
cv_predictions$Logistic_One_Class <- factor(
  ifelse(
    cv_predictions$Logistic_One_Probability > 0.5,
    "1",
    "0"
  ),
  levels = c("0", "1")
)

cv_predictions$Logistic_Two_Class <- factor(
  ifelse(
    cv_predictions$Logistic_Two_Probability > 0.5,
    "1",
    "0"
  ),
  levels = c("0", "1")
)

cv_predictions$NB_One_Class <- factor(
  ifelse(
    cv_predictions$NB_One_Probability > 0.5,
    "1",
    "0"
  ),
  levels = c("0", "1")
)

cv_predictions$NB_Two_Class <- factor(
  ifelse(
    cv_predictions$NB_Two_Probability > 0.5,
    "1",
    "0"
  ),
  levels = c("0", "1")
)

# Function for calculating performance from pooled held-out predictions
calculate_cv_metrics <- function(
    truth,
    predicted,
    probability
) {
  truth <- factor(
    truth,
    levels = c("0", "1")
  )

  predicted <- factor(
    predicted,
    levels = c("0", "1")
  )

  TP <- sum(truth == "1" & predicted == "1")
  TN <- sum(truth == "0" & predicted == "0")
  FP <- sum(truth == "0" & predicted == "1")
  FN <- sum(truth == "1" & predicted == "0")

  accuracy <- (TP + TN) / length(truth)
  sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)
  specificity <- TN / (TN + FP)
  precision <- TP / (TP + FP)
  false_discovery_rate <- FP / (TP + FP)
  false_positive_rate <- FP / (FP + TN)

  f1_score <- (
    2 * precision * sensitivity /
      (precision + sensitivity)
  )

  # Rank-based calculation of ROC AUC
  n_positive <- sum(truth == "1")
  n_negative <- sum(truth == "0")

  probability_ranks <- rank(
    probability,
    ties.method = "average"
  )

  roc_auc <- (
    sum(probability_ranks[truth == "1"]) -
      n_positive * (n_positive + 1) / 2
  ) / (
    n_positive * n_negative
  )

  data.frame(
    Accuracy = 100 * accuracy,
    Sensitivity = 100 * sensitivity,
    Specificity = 100 * specificity,
    Precision = 100 * precision,
    F1 = 100 * f1_score,
    FDR = 100 * false_discovery_rate,
    FPR = 100 * false_positive_rate,
    ROC_AUC = roc_auc
  )
}

performance_table <- rbind(
  cbind(
    Model = "Logistic regression: one gene",
    calculate_cv_metrics(
      cv_predictions$Truth,
      cv_predictions$Logistic_One_Class,
      cv_predictions$Logistic_One_Probability
    )
  ),
  cbind(
    Model = "Logistic regression: two genes",
    calculate_cv_metrics(
      cv_predictions$Truth,
      cv_predictions$Logistic_Two_Class,
      cv_predictions$Logistic_Two_Probability
    )
  ),
  cbind(
    Model = "Naive Bayes: one gene",
    calculate_cv_metrics(
      cv_predictions$Truth,
      cv_predictions$NB_One_Class,
      cv_predictions$NB_One_Probability
    )
  ),
  cbind(
    Model = "Naive Bayes: two genes",
    calculate_cv_metrics(
      cv_predictions$Truth,
      cv_predictions$NB_Two_Class,
      cv_predictions$NB_Two_Probability
    )
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  performance_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Patient-Grouped Cross-Validation Performance",
    "for Four Classification Models"
  )
)
```

```{r extra_credit_subtype}
for (fold in 1:5) {

  # Select genes using only this fold's training patients
  fold_pvals <- apply(
    ec_ge[, fit_rows, drop = FALSE],
    1,
    function(values) {
      tryCatch(
        t.test(values ~ ec_outcome[fit_rows])$p.value,
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
    }
  )

  ranked_genes <- names(sort(fold_pvals))
  stopifnot(length(ranked_genes) >= 2)

  selected <- ranked_genes[1:2]
  ec_selected_genes[[fold]] <- selected

  fold_data <- data.frame(
    Subtype = ec_outcome,
    gene1 = as.numeric(ec_ge[selected[1], ]),
    gene2 = as.numeric(ec_ge[selected[2], ])
  )

  # Learn scaling from training patients only
  predictors <- c("gene1", "gene2")

  scaled_fit <- scale(
    fold_data[fit_rows, predictors, drop = FALSE]
  )

  fold_data[, predictors] <- scale(
    fold_data[, predictors, drop = FALSE],
    center = attr(scaled_fit, "scaled:center"),
    scale = attr(scaled_fit, "scaled:scale")
  )

  model_br <- glm(
    Subtype ~ gene1 + gene2,
    data = fold_data[fit_rows, , drop = FALSE],
    family = binomial(),
    method = brglm2::brglmFit,
    control = brglm2::brglmControl(
      type = "AS_mean",
      maxit = 1000
    )
  )

  ec_converged[fold] <- isTRUE(model_br$converged)

  if (!ec_converged[fold]) {
    stop("Model did not converge in fold ", fold)
  }

  ec_probability_br[validation_rows] <- predict(
    model_br,
    newdata = fold_data[validation_rows, , drop = FALSE],
    type = "response"
  )
}

stopifnot(all(ec_converged), !anyNA(ec_probability_br))

ec_predicted_br <- factor(
  as.numeric(ec_probability_br > 0.5),
  levels = c(0, 1)
)

ec_confusion <- table(
  Actual = ec_info$Subtype_Group,
  Predicted = factor(
    ec_predicted_br,
    levels = c("0", "1"),
    labels = c("Luminal", "Basal")
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  ec_confusion,
  caption = "Subtype classification: cross-validated predictions"
)

ec_metrics <- calculate_cv_metrics(
  truth = ec_outcome,
  predicted = ec_predicted_br,
  probability = ec_probability_br
)

knitr::kable(
  ec_metrics,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Subtype classification performance; Basal is positive"
)

# Display genes selected in each fold
ec_gene_table <- data.frame(
  Fold = rep(1:5, each = 2),
  Gene_ID = unlist(ec_selected_genes, use.names = FALSE)
)

ec_gene_table$Symbol <- gene_info$gene_name[
  match(
    sub("\\..*$", "", ec_gene_table$Gene_ID),
    sub("\\..*$", "", gene_info$gene_id)
  )
]

knitr::kable(
  ec_gene_table,
  caption = "Genes selected using each fold's training patients"
)

data.frame(
  Fold = 1:5,
  Converged = ec_converged
)
```
There was 92.9% accuracy, however, only 64.7% Basal sensitivity versus 98.8% Luminal specificity. This model missed 6 of 17 Basal tumors.
